LESSON: SWIMMING (OPTIONAL)

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Performing and Displaying
Topic 2.6: Swimming (Optional)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Swimming (Optional), part of Performing and Displaying in Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: Why is Swimming an essential life skill?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise ways of water entry in the swimming pool,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Swimming (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. play water games in the swimming pool for fun,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Swimming (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. float in water for skill acquisition,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Swimming (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. glide in water for water confidence,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Swimming (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate safety in and out of the swimming pool while playing water games.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Swimming (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. recognise ways of water entry in the swimming pool,

   Swimming (Optional) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. play water games in the swimming pool for fun,

   Swimming (Optional) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. float in water for skill acquisition,

   Swimming (Optional) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. glide in water for water confidence,

   Swimming (Optional) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. appreciate safety in and out of the swimming pool while playing water games.

   Swimming (Optional) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. visit the swimming pool for familiarisation and water orientation,

2. demonstrate water entry into the pool

3. use feet first technique,

4. collaboratively, engage in different water games while observing safety,

5. demonstrate floating techniques,

6. practise floating technique while observing safety,

7. demonstrate gliding in water, observing safety,

8. practise gliding,

9. observe each other performing the glide and floating and provide feedback.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. visit the swimming pool for familiarisation and water orientation,
2. demonstrate water entry into the pool
3. use feet first technique,
4. collaboratively, engage in different water games while observing safety,
5. demonstrate floating techniques,
6. practise floating technique while observing safety,
7. demonstrate gliding in water, observing safety,
8. practise gliding,
9. observe each other performing the glide and floating and provide feedback.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Swimming (Optional) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: The learner builds confidence by floating in water.

• Learning to learn: The learner acquires the skills of pool entry and floating in water.

Values:
• Respect: The learner respects others' performance in floating and gliding in water.

• Responsibility: The learner observes own and others safety while performing and practising the water entry, floating and

gliding.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Safety and security: The learner adheres to water safety precautions while practising water entry, floating and gliding.

• Environmental awareness: The learner familiarises with the pool environment, safe use of water and pool hygiene.

Link to other learning areas:

Science and Technology: The learner develops a practical understanding of correct body posture when floating and gliding.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. recognise ways of water entry in the swimming pool,
2. play water games in the swimming pool for fun,
3. float in water for skill acquisition,
4. glide in water for water confidence,
5. appreciate safety in and out of the swimming pool while playing water games.

Remember the key question: Why is Swimming an essential life skill?
